DECODE R2120.summary: Van Dedem, Dutch ambassador at Constantinople, reports to Grand Pensionary Van de Spiegel the Porte's proposed loan of 7-8 million, secured on the revenues of Morea, Negropont, Salonica, Volos, Urfan, Cara Agatz, Damascus, Sorien and Rodosto and the tribute of Jenischeher, and suggests the Levant Directors or Hope & Co. take it up. The decryption is the contemporary clear decipherment filed as R2121.
DECODE R2120.en:
Dated 22 December 1788. Missive of Mr van Dedem van de Gelder.

Right Honourable Sir! In a subsequent negotiation with the Reis Effendi, the Kaymakam, and the Kâhya Bey, lieutenant of
the Grand Vizier, of State, I gave him to understand, first, that however much I could assure him that Their High
Mightinesses continue to be most strongly attached to the interests of this Court, and show themselves inclined on every
occasion to give tokens of their true sentiments and sincere friendship, I must nevertheless forewarn him that I did not
at all believe that Their High Mightinesses could or would charge themselves with the direct execution of the proposal he
had made;

DECODE R2122.summary: Two cipher blocks (258 groups) in a clear letter to Van de Spiegel, decoded in part with the block-alphabetical table of the second pass; the firm words (envoyé, Porta, negociatie, Republicq, Leening) are consistent with the loan theme of the R2121 crib. Values, not sense: the running reading is fragmentary.
DECODE R2122.en:
Duplicate. High Noble Honourable Sir!

Being of the view that the interest and political system of Their High Mightinesses and that of [1230] their two new
allies and [1330] the present state of affairs, through the resolution of the second of October, must more than ever
before be held to be one and the same, all my démarches, both at the Porte and elsewhere, which until the receipt of
that resolution, for want of the [?troops'] instruction, had to remain largely idle, have since then been regulated in
every respect; and having the advantage of perceiving most clearly on every occasion [that] the whole Ministry places
a particular trust in me, I can assure Your Honour (in truth) [that] my insinuations have been of no good effect, and I
do not doubt whether, if continued, they will be reckoned of enough importance to find acceptance.

DECODE R2131.summary: One cipher paragraph of 50 groups in a clear letter to Van de Spiegel, decoded in part (16 of 46 non-null groups firm); it names the Porte, an envoy, the war and the French, but the neutrality reading proposed in review is not established.
DECODE R2131.en:
I have the honour to inform Your Honour [?that] the Ottoman Porte, the day before yesterday, [?bound] itself fully to
the Prussian envoy to keep itself neutral in [?all] [?respects] during this war with the French, without entering into
any further alliance [with] the aforesaid nation.

snip.cap: R2122, 15 January 1789: the opening groups 2504 2604 2704 recur in the other letters

system: A homophonic one-word-per-group code, numbers 2-3839, shared with Van Dedem's 1789 French despatches; R1895 (1799) uses a different marked system.
